baseline._about: Words the learner already knows, from Kotlin, everyday Android work, or the Android course.

avoid._about: Words a beginner misreads or that hide who does what.

phrases.the system: name the actor: the kernel, SurfaceFlinger, ART
phrases.just a: cut it, or say what it is

call stack.def: The chain of function calls a thread is inside right now, from the first caller to the running function.

sample.def: A snapshot of a thread's call stack, taken by the kernel every so many CPU events.

method tracing.def: Recording a timestamp at the start and end of every method call, by instrumenting the code.

instrumentation.def: Extra code injected into your app to record what it does; it slows the app down.

trace section.def: A named span you mark yourself with trace("name") { }, recorded in a system trace.

call chart.def: Each call drawn as a bar along a timeline, callees under their caller.

flame chart.def: The call chart with identical call stacks merged; width is total time, not a timeline.

self time.def: Time a function spent running its own code, not the functions it called.

total time.def: Self time plus the time spent in everything the function called.

thread state.def: What a thread is doing according to the kernel: running, runnable, sleeping, or in uninterruptible sleep.

Running.def: The thread is on a CPU, executing.

Runnable.def: The thread is ready to run but waiting for a free CPU.

Sleeping.def: The thread is waiting for something: a lock, a Binder reply, a message.

Uninterruptible Sleep.def: The thread is waiting inside the kernel, usually for disk I/O.

FrameTimeline.def: Perfetto's view of every frame: when it was expected to finish and when it really did.

Expected Timeline.def: The time window the app was given to render a frame.

Actual Timeline.def: When the app's frame work really started and ended, GPU included.

deadline.def: The end of a frame's expected window: finish after it and the frame is late.

Concurrent Copying.def: ART's default garbage collector since Android 8: it moves live objects while your threads keep running.

TLAB.def: A thread's own slice of the heap; allocating there is a pointer bump, with no lock.

young GC.def: A collection of only recently created objects, which mostly die young; cheap and frequent.

allocation churn.def: Creating many short-lived objects, which makes the collector run often.

heap dump.def: A snapshot of every object in the app's heap and who refers to whom.

GC root.def: A starting point the collector always keeps: a thread's local variables, static fields, and the like.

shallow size.def: The memory one object takes by itself.

retained size.def: The memory that would be freed if this object were freed: itself plus all it alone keeps alive.

leak.def: An object that's no longer needed but is still reachable from a GC root, so it's never freed.
